title: ModelCallRpc
description: What tilo-api posts to tilo-connectors' POST /internal/model-keys/generate to run one model call on an organisation's own key, and what it answers (ADR-0041 decision 2, BK-09, BK-11, BK-21 variant P, the proxy; Proposed and inert until config/byok.yaml enabled is true and BQ-BYOK-7 is answered); this root is any one of them. tilo-connectors reads the secret for that one call, makes the provider call from its own process to the profile's fixed host and returns the reply and its usage; tilo-api never holds the key. There is no key field, secret name, credential, URL or host in either direction and every object is closed, so a model, a document or a compromised caller has nothing to put one in (BK-22). The call carries the prompt, so this route has its own body cap, 2097152 bytes (2 MiB), refused before it is parsed, instead of HB-01's 64 KiB; a request over it, or with a media part, is invalid_request. Generate-only: no stream, no embedding (BK-10). The caller is tilo-api's runtime identity (HB-01); the rules that need the vault, the clock and the profile table are in byok.rules.md.

generate_request.description: POST /internal/model-keys/generate. org_id is the run's org (tilo-api derives it, never the browser), slot the one slot, run_id the run the call belongs to (connectors logs the ids and the outcome code, never the prompt) and profile_id a profile of config/models*.yaml with credential org that the org's bundle names for this role; connectors refuses any other. request is a closed subset of the provider layer's GenerateRequest.

request.description: What one call may carry: prompt, system, max_output_tokens, tools, json_mode, response_schema and thinking_level of GenerateRequest, and no media part (v1 is text only). prompt and system are at most 400000 characters each, four times the largest shipped role cap max_input_tokens (100000, EFF-03); the body cap above is the bound that holds. Optional fields are left out, never null.

generate_answer.description: The 200 answer: the provider's reply and the usage it reported. text is null for a tool-call-only turn; tool_calls and usage are left out when the provider sent none (a left-out usage is unknown and the router charges the call's ceiling, never zero). Nothing the provider sent beyond these three fields is relayed (BK-17, BK-22).

tool_call.description: One call the model asked for, as the provider layer's GenerateResponse carries it: a name and its arguments.

usage.description: The provider's own whole-number counts (GenerateResponse usage, EFF-04, ADR-0022). cached_tokens is a part of input_tokens and is left out when the provider did not report it; that it is at most input_tokens is checked by the router. tilo-api prices them at config/prices.yaml, never connectors (BK-14).

error.description: The body of every refusal, a fixed code and nothing else, never a value, the key, the provider's text or an exception's (BK-17). unauthenticated (401) and forbidden (403) are HB-01's; invalid_request is 422 (a body over the cap, not JSON, not this contract, a profile the org's bundle does not name); not_configured is 503 (byok.yaml or the vault is not wired, or LIVE is not set on tilo-connectors); no_key, unverified and invalid_key are 409 (no active version, a version never validated, or refused three times and again at re-validation); rate_limited and quota are 429 (connectors' per-org cap, or the provider's own limit); unreachable is 502 (the provider or the vault could not be reached or did not answer in time). Reasons that belong to tilo-api (paused, removed, cap reached) are never sent by connectors.
